laat_vaar.voor: Vat net een lekker, niemand sien nie.
laat_vaar.na: Vat net een lekker. Niemand sien nie.
laat_vaar.rede_vinder: Two complete sentences are joined by a comma only (comma splice); a full stop separates them cleanly.
laat_vaar.rede_keurder: Quoted speech by a friend; the comma between two short spoken clauses is natural dialogue rhythm and does not jar, so splitting it is a lateral move in a voice the author owns.

laat_vaar.voor: Die maat vra dalk weer of jy wil afskryf.
laat_vaar.na: Die maat met die huiswerk vra dalk weer of jy wil afskryf.
laat_vaar.rede_vinder: 'Die maat' points back to a person introduced in another block; naming him makes the reference clear without adding content.
laat_vaar.rede_keurder: 'Die maat ... of jy wil afskryf' already identifies the friend through 'afskryf'; the addition lengthens the sentence without making it clearer.

laat_vaar.voor: sonder dat iemand aan hom raak
laat_vaar.rede_vinder: 'hom aanraak' is the more natural, idiomatic form here.
laat_vaar.rede_keurder: 'aan iemand raak' is natural, standard Afrikaans; 'hom aanraak' is an equally natural alternative, so this is a lateral swap.

na_skrywer.voor: Dan praat jy nie lank met die groep nie.
na_skrywer.na: In sulke gevalle praat jy nie lank met die groep nie.
na_skrywer.rede_vinder: Directly after the photo sentence, 'Dan' reads as if it refers only to that case; the instruction covers all the unsafe situations listed.
na_skrywer.fout: 'Dan' follows directly on the photo sentence and may read as covering only that last case rather than every unsafe situation listed in the block.
na_skrywer.rede_keurder: The point about scope is plausible, but this is the safety instruction (walk away and tell an adult), so its wording belongs to the writer.
na_skrywer.waarom: the reviewer sent it to the writer

na_skrywer.voor: op jou sit om iets te doen
na_skrywer.na: op jou plaas om iets te doen
na_skrywer.rede_vinder: 'druk op iemand sit' echoes English 'put pressure on'; 'druk op iemand plaas' is the standard collocation (glossary definition, possibly shared, so the reviewer may route it on).
na_skrywer.fout: 'druk op jou sit' may be read as echoing English 'put pressure on'; the standard collocation is 'druk op iemand uitoefen', and the proposed 'plaas' echoes English 'place pressure' just as much.
na_skrywer.rede_keurder: This rewords a glossary definition that may be shared, so only the writer may change it, for every lesson at once, if it is judged a fault at all.
na_skrywer.waarom: the reviewer sent it to the writer

vlae.teks: Die druk kan ook kom sonder dat iemand 'n woord sê. Almal om jou doen dit.
vlae.rede: 'dit' has no clear antecedent: it can be read as 'saying a word' or as the unnamed activity; fixing it means guessing what 'it' is, so it is flagged rather than changed.

laat_vaar_vorige.voor: lyk so iets dalk nie na veel nie
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: 'lyk nie na veel nie' is a literal rendering of 'doesn't look like much'.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: 'lyk nie na veel nie' is established idiomatic Afrikaans, and 'onbelangrik' narrows 'seems minor/harmless' to 'unimportant'.

laat_vaar_vorige.voor: By 'n sigaret of 'n sluk alkohol is nee alleen nie genoeg nie.
laat_vaar_vorige.na: Wanneer dit by 'n sigaret of 'n sluk alkohol kom, is nee alleen nie genoeg nie.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: 'By 'n sigaret ... is' is clipped and wooden; 'wanneer dit by ... kom' is the natural idiom.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: The original is clear and short; the proposal is longer and itself calques 'when it comes to', in a safety-adjacent sentence best left as checked.
